question: Which of the listed transitions are permitted by the rules? Return their IDs.
annotationRubric: Label only explicit atomic episodes in supplied visible reasoning. Each label has a verbatim contiguous quote, zero-based occurrence, category, concluded atom and explicitly stated ordered premises. Categories: premise_consumed (uses established evidence without proving it again), positive_derivation (an actual supported inference), absence_recheck (explicit argument that a path or transition is absent), new_residual (a supported inference about the current downstream obligation), arithmetic (resource/objective computation), ambiguous (unsupported or unclear). Relations: edge, path, ready. ready ID requires both paths of that needs row. Atom and premise endpoints must appear literally in the quote. No edges or premises may be supplied from your own source knowledge. A reference/assertion alone is not a derivation. For arithmetic and ambiguous, atom and premises may be empty. Do not infer unexposed reasoning. Do not add labels merely to populate a category. Do not repair wrong IDs. Include explicit negative reasoning, but do not infer absence from missing text. You are not given arm, score or cost; supplied reasoning can still reveal its condition. Return labels in text order. Completeness is not guaranteed.
annotationRules: Exact nonoverlapping quotes; endpoint literals; independent finite truth; explicit ordered edge/path chain or ready conjunction for positive inference. premise_consumed must refer to an earlier or supplied true atom. new_residual is derived by classification after validation, never trusted from label name. A repeated positive atom is counted across different questions in the same source scope. Exact-premise repeat reported separately. Negative claims require an explicit negative argument and independently absent atom, but completeness of the quoted absence argument is unproven. Arithmetic and ambiguity are reported without assigning cached-atom savings. Rejected/empty/missing labels remain visible. Two blind passes of the SAME model are correlated annotations, not independent-rater validation.

claims.correctReuse: Equal native support nodes across different obligations; source/handle binding and independent answer agreement.
claims.reducedRepetition: Requires directly supported baseline repetitions plus validated annotation coverage; native hits alone are insufficient.
claims.newInference: Distinct correct downstream answers and qualified nonsupplied consequences after the first obligation. No optimization or depth claim.

controls: Same task, sibling schedule, history policy, answer schema and input-plus-all-output cap. No pruning, ranking, optimal answer or anti-repetition instruction. Fact and Scheme supply identical atomic outcomes; Scheme adds checked ancestor-closed fragments. Unused reservations are censored, not savings. All failed calls and unknown usage retained.
